title: A crash loop is systemd retrying, not systemd failing
explanation: `systemctl status webapp` reporting `activating (auto-restart)` means `Restart=always` in the unit is silently relaunching the process after every crash. Recognizing this state up front matters: it tells you the *unit definition* is probably fine, and the real fault is something happening at the process's own startup, every single time.

title: Ask the process why it's dying, not the supervisor
explanation: systemd only knows the process exited non-zero — it has no idea why. The process's own stderr/stdout, captured by journald, usually has the actual reason spelled out in plain text. `journalctl -u webapp -n 20 --no-pager` is where that reason lives, not `systemctl status` alone.

title: Trace the error to its real source before editing anything
explanation: The log line `FATAL: LISTEN_PORT must be a number, got: 'eighty'` points at the *application's config*, not the unit file. Confirming this distinction matters because editing `webapp.service` (the wrong layer) would change nothing — the fault is a bad value in `/etc/webapp/webapp.conf`.

title: Fix the value at its source, then restart
explanation: Because only the application's own config changed — not the systemd unit file itself — a plain `systemctl restart webapp` is enough. Reaching for `daemon-reload` out of habit here would be a no-op: that command re-reads unit *definitions*, which were never the problem, and reaching for it anyway can obscure which change actually fixed things.

title: Confirm the loop genuinely stopped, not just paused between crashes
explanation: A single `active` reading taken right after a restart can catch a crash-looping service mid-cycle, between one death and the next. Checking `systemctl is-active webapp` again after a few seconds (or watching it hold steady) is how you tell "genuinely fixed" apart from "currently in the up phase of the same loop."
